missing_element: Clinical documentation is strong but narrative doesn't explicitly state that this was an anaphylactic reaction requiring ALS assessment and intervention. Cigna's denial appears to be based on the fact that patient self-administered epinephrine before EMS arrival.
appeal_strategy: Submitted appeal emphasizing: (1) anaphylaxis is a life-threatening emergency requiring ALS monitoring regardless of pre-arrival treatment, (2) EMS administered two additional medications (diphenhydramine IV, epinephrine IM) which are ALS-level interventions, (3) biphasic anaphylaxis risk required continuous ALS monitoring during transport, (4) cited Cigna's own clinical policy on anaphylaxis management. Attached medication administration record and vital sign trending.

timeline.title: Denial received — CO-18
timeline.detail: Duplicate claim/service. An identical claim has already been processed.

timeline.title: Closed — no appeal needed
timeline.detail: $1,800 written off.

payer_notes.text: Called Aetna provider services. Representative confirmed the denial (CO-18) is documentation-based and directed us to file a first-level appeal with the PCR attached.

Verified that original claim was paid. This was a duplicate submission error from the billing system. No appeal needed — confirmed payment on original claim. Flagged billing system to prevent duplicate submissions.

denial_reason_text: Not medically necessary. Documentation does not support emergency ambulance transport.
pcr_narrative_excerpt: Responded to 911 call at private residence. 55-year-old male reports back pain for 3 days, worsening today. No acute distress. Vitals all within normal limits. No neurological deficits. Patient ambulatory. Transported to hospital per patient request.
missing_element: Patient was stable, ambulatory, with a chronic complaint (3 days of back pain). No emergency medical condition documented. Transport appears to be for patient convenience rather than medical necessity.
appeal_strategy: Attempted appeal citing patient's 911 call and reported pain level. Denied on second review. Payer position: non-acute back pain in an ambulatory patient does not meet medical necessity criteria for emergency ambulance transport. Patient should have used private vehicle or non-emergency transport. Reviewed with crew — this was a patient-convenience transport that should have been documented differently.

appeal_letter:
Date: 2026-08-31
To: Anthem BCBS — Appeals Department
Re: Denial of BLS Emergency transport · CPT A0428 · DOS 2026-08-08 · CO-50

To whom it may concern,

We are formally appealing the denial of the above claim, denied with the reason: "Not medically necessary. Documentation does not support emergency ambulance transport."

The transport was medically necessary and properly documented. Attempted appeal citing patient's 911 call and reported pain level. Denied on second review. Payer position: non-acute back pain in an ambulatory patient does not meet medical necessity criteria for emergency ambulance transport. Patient should have used private vehicle or non-emergency transport. Reviewed with crew — this was a patient-convenience transport that should have been documented differently.

We respectfully request reprocessing and payment of $1,200. The patient care report, physician documentation, and applicable medical-necessity criteria are attached.

Sincerely,
Ambra Revenue Recovery — Appeals Team

payer_notes.text: Called Anthem BCBS provider services. Representative confirmed the denial (CO-50) is documentation-based and directed us to file a first-level appeal with the PCR attached.
First-level appeal uploaded to the Anthem BCBS provider portal with the PCR and medical-necessity statement.
Payer response received: Appeal upheld — denial stands, $850 recovered.

denial_reason_text: Missing information needed for adjudication. Patient insurance information does not match records on file.
pcr_narrative_excerpt: Emergency response to public park for 40-year-old female who fainted during outdoor event. Patient regained consciousness before EMS arrival. Vitals: BP 92/60, HR 54, blood glucose 68 mg/dL. Orthostatic hypotension confirmed. IV established, normal saline bolus. Transported to ED for evaluation.
missing_element: Patient's insurance ID number on the claim did not match Cigna's records. Patient had recently changed plans during open enrollment — old member ID was used instead of new one.
appeal_strategy: Obtained correct member ID from patient. Resubmitted claim with updated insurance information. Claim processed and paid on resubmission. Flagged process: verify member ID at time of billing for patients with recent plan changes.
